---
title: "Unsupervised learning"
---

Explore patterns in data without using class labels to construct the representation or clusters.

## Principal component analysis

Principal component analysis (PCA) finds directions along which the data vary most. By projecting the data onto a few of these directions, we can explore a lower-dimensional view of its structure.

- [Explore how PCA chooses a direction](pca-explorer.qmd)
- [Work through the gas-sensor PCA notebook](01-pca-gas-sensor-array.ipynb)

## K-means clustering

K-means groups observations around a chosen number of cluster centers. Explore how the centers move, then fit models and compare different choices of $K$ in the notebook.

- [Step through k-means clustering](kmeans-explorer.qmd)
- [Work through the k-means notebook](02-kmeans-clustering.ipynb)

## Hierarchical clustering

Agglomerative hierarchical clustering builds nested groups by merging observations or existing clusters. The resulting dendrogram lets us inspect the full hierarchy before choosing where to cut it into final clusters.

- [Step through hierarchical clustering on two moons](hierarchical-clustering-explorer.qmd)
- [Work through the hierarchical-clustering notebook](03-hierarchical-clustering.ipynb)

## Density-based clustering

Density-based clustering groups observations that lie in dense regions of the data, while identifying isolated observations as noise. Explore how DBSCAN builds clusters without specifying their number in advance.

- [Step through DBSCAN on concentric circles](dbscan-explorer.qmd)
- [Work through the DBSCAN notebook](04-dbscan-clustering.ipynb)
